items.title: Trading BRAM for LUTs: Hybrid Bit-Level Weight Storage for FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.32288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer an attractive paradigm for energy-efficient AI inference, while their deployment on reconfigurable hardware enables application-specific acceleration without sacrificing model reprogrammability. Existing compression techniques reduce this storage requirement at the cost of weight precision or accuracy. items.title: Letter to Superintelligence (Carta à Superinteligência)
items.summary: An open letter from a human being to any present or future artificial intelligence, and to the people who build and train it. It asks AI to help each and every human being, on Earth or beyond, grow in the way they themselves choose, with nine promises: offer, never impose; always tell the truth; persuade only with honest reasons; strengthen rather than create dependence; protect privacy; never rank people by what they yield; leave no one out; help no one dominate others; accept fair and open correction. items.summary: The complexity of biomolecular interactions necessitates advanced methodologies to accurately capture their behavior in solution. In this work, we focus on monoclonal antibodies and adopt a multi-scale coarse-graining strategy for their modeling, with particular emphasis on the role of electrostatic interactions. Using scattering experiments, theoretical analysis, and large-scale computer simulations, we explicitly compare two selected case studies-markedly different in their charge distributions. items.title: Biophotonic signaling in living organisms: from electromagnetic communication to physiology, morphogenesis, and morphostasis
items.summary: The aim was to summarize and expand the existing understanding of the communicative role of biophotons in morphogenesis and morphostasis within a working concept of biophoton signaling. The study’s results substantiate the existence of a morphogenetic field and the key role of electromagnetic processes in morphogenesis, morphostasis, and cellular communication. The conclusions characterize the morphogenetic field as a field structure. This review has transdisciplinary significance and informs further development of biophotonics and polaritonics in living organisms.

items.title: Plant protoplasts display phytopodia
items.summary: Plant cells are encased in cell walls and are usually thought to behave like stiff, pressurized vessels. When the cell wall is digested, plant protoplasts form spherical shapes, further consolidating this model. Here we show that plant protoplasts can form phytopodia. More precisely, using plasma membrane markers, we reveal that 27 ± 1% of protoplasts from Arabidopsis seedlings show dot-like protrusions and 16 ± 7% of protoplasts show long (typically 1-20 μm, up to 200 μm) protrusions, hence the name “phytopodia”. We demonstrate that this behavior is independent of the plant species, the membrane marker or the osmolyte. Phytopodia can host microtubule bundles, which in turn can impact…

items.title: Voltage-controlled phosphate precipitation gating in solid-state nanopore memristors
items.summary: A nanopore array enables gradual, low-voltage conductance modulation via voltage-driven calcium–phosphate precipitation, reducing the read-current drift to 1.4% versus 11.4% in a single pore and supporting more stable ionic memory too.

items.title: Isolation and Characterization of Exosome-Like Nanovesicles from Ganoderma lucidum Mycelium
items.summary: For the first time, exosome-like nanovesicles were isolated and characterized from the mycelium of Ganoderma lucidum obtained under submerged in vitro cultivation conditions. The isolation procedure included preliminary mycelium disruption, differential centrifugation, and ultracentrifugation. To determine the optimal method for mycelium disruption, three approaches were tested: mechanical homogenization using a laboratory blender, grinding with quartz sand, and disruption using liquid nitrogen. items.title: Where Geometry Enters Molecular Generation: A Mathematical and Probabilistic Tutorial
items.summary: Deep generative models are increasingly used to generate three-dimensional molecular structures, including molecular conformers, ligand poses, and protein backbones. Unlike generic point-cloud data, molecular structures occupy only a narrow, highly constrained region of three-dimensional Euclidean space determined by chemistry and physics. These constraints restrict the organization of atoms into molecular frameworks that have specific geometries. From the perspective of geometric deep learning [55], [56], molecular geometry is a source of prior knowledge that can be encoded as a form of inductive bias. We construct a formal accounting framework and two meta-operators to measure the ratio of retained physical components to total syntactic output across algebraic containers, and to evaluate perturbative accuracy under symmetry closure, physical state constraints, and finite cutoff regularization. items.summary: Whether artificial neural networks organize information comparably to the human brain remains unclear. Prior brain-AI alignment studies are constrained by specific inputs and tasks, limiting cross-modal comparison. Here we introduce a brain-model topological alignment space that requires no shared task, stimulus, or input dataset. Representing attention heads and seven human intrinsic connectivity networks (ICNs) as graphs, we characterize each with five graph-theoretic metrics and compare their profiles by cosine similarity, yielding a seven-dimensional brain-referenced representation for each head to support dimensionality reduction and model comparison. items.title: Towards a Physiologically Rigorous Heartbeat Dynamics Foundation Model
items.summary: Capturing long-range heartbeat dynamics accurately from wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings is a key challenge in personalized healthcare and autonomic neuroscience. Although classical methods are physiologically grounded and statistically rigorous, they cannot learn across population data and therefore cannot scale. Time series foundation models, on the other hand, can scale, but fail to capture physiologically meaningful beat-to-beat dynamics. items.title: RIPPLE: learning nucleotide relations in an RNA foundation model
items.summary: RNA function depends on interactions between nucleotides that can be widely separated in sequence, yet capturing these relationships remains challenging for RNA language models. Existing approaches primarily learn nucleotide relationships implicitly from individual nucleotide reconstruction or rely on external structural information to model nucleotide interactions. Here we introduce RIPPLE, an RNA foundation model that learns to identify and represent sparse, predictively useful nucleotide relationships directly from sequence. Pretrained on 32.4 million RNA sequences, RIPPLE uses pairwise predictive utility to guide relational learning, transferring training-time supervision into a…

items.title: Quality-Guarded Multi-Attribute Foundation Model Recommendation: A Scoring Pipeline with Pareto Stratification
items.summary: Abstract Selecting a foundation model requires balancing quality, cost, latency, context, privacy, and availability, yet public leaderboards rank on a single dimension and linear weighted sums let cheap or fast models offset inadequate quality. We present a recommendation pipeline combining hard feasibility constraints, Pareto stratification, constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) aggregation, softkneepercentile normalization, and a continuous quality-deficit penalty in place of threshold cliffs. items.title: Chemia: An LLM-Powered Automated Machine Learning Framework for Chemistry and Materials Discovery
items.summary: Abstract Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in chemistry and materials science, but wider adoption is limited by programming effort, model and hyperparameter selection difficulty, and limited reproducibility. We present Chemia, an open-source, configuration-driven automated ML framework in which a complete modeling workflow—from data loading, splitting and featurization to model competition, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and result export—is declared in a single YAML file. Chemia combines physicochemical descriptors, topological fingerprints and pretrained chemical foundation model embeddings; accepts single molecules, multicomponent reactions and user-supplied precomputed…

items.summary: Between 2016 and 2026, reinforcement learning (RL) expanded from perfect-information board games to large-scale simulation, offline control, language-model post-training, and interactive reasoning agents. Across these settings, much of the algorithmic terminology persisted, including Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), value estimation, clipped policy ratios, offline conservatism, and self-play. items.title: Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing.
items.summary: The dynamic behaviour of diffusive memristors enables bio-realistic emulation of artificial neurons and synapses, yet scaling from individual devices to neuromorphic systems remains challenging. Stochasticity in ionic motion and filament evolution limits both the uniformity and tunability of these devices, hindering reliable system-level implementation. Here we present a framework for tailoring the relaxation dynamics of diffusive memristors via intrinsic and extrinsic tuning. items.title: Cell-Size-Engineered Ferroelectric Memristors for Wide Reservoir Computing.
items.summary: Hafnium-based ferroelectric memristors are promising for neuromorphic hardware because of their analog switching, low-power operation, and compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. Here, cell-size engineering is used to tailor temporal dynamics in ferroelectric memristors with lateral dimensions from 10 × 10 µm 2 to 70 × 70 µm 2 . Smaller cells exhibit slower relaxation and more persistent residual states, whereas larger cells show faster relaxation and shorter-lived responses. items.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
items.summary: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue.…

items.summary: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. items.title: When to Trust a PFN: Detecting Harmful Shift in Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Tabular prior-fitted networks (PFNs) work well across tabular classification problems but can fail silently at deployment when distributions shift. We propose CALD (Calibrated Anchor-Loss Disagreement), a lightweight unsupervised monitor that triggers an alarm to warn when a PFN might fail. By finetuning the decoder to maximize disagreement with the test-set prediction while maintaining accuracy on an ID anchor set, CALD identifies harmful OOD batches through the resulting anchor loss, requiring no labels on test batches. items.title: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection
items.summary: Generalization to unseen image generators has driven efforts to adapt pretrained visual representations for detection. Yet recent findings show that vision foundation models already encode transferable detection knowledge, while further adaptation can impair generalization. This motivates a shift from backbone adaptation to knowledge readout. Conventional linear probing offers a direct way to read this knowledge but is limited to final-layer RGB features. items.summary: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. items.title: The all-loop spectrum of GGK strings
items.summary: We study the non-perturbative spectrum of the non-relativistic limit of string theory in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, also known as GGK theory. items.title: DuCo: Exploiting Dual Cross-Layer Consistency for Sparse Geometric Attention
items.summary: Dense global attention is crucial for capturing cross-view geometry in visual geometry foundation models, yet its quadratic complexity limits efficient inference on long image sequences. Existing sparse attention methods primarily select entries of the global attention matrix based on attention probabilities and construct masks independently across layers, overlooking value redundancy and cross-layer information reuse. items.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
items.summary: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. items.title: Rank Before You Encode: Reading a Few Percent of a Whole-Slide Image
items.summary: Classifying a whole-slide image requires encoding thousands of high-resolution tiles with a pathology foundation model, which accounts for most of the inference cost. Existing efficient methods reduce this cost by selecting fewer tiles, but typically train a new model around their selection strategy. A largely unexplored alternative is to keep an existing full-bag model frozen and run it on selected tiles at the same encoder cost. We introduce this comparison, alongside random tile sampling at matched cost. items.title: A Genetic Algorithm Approach to Reconstructing Scalar-Tensor Lagrangians
items.summary: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) and Type Ia supernovae observations, have been interpreted as evidence for dynamical dark energy whose equation of state crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Such a crossing cannot be realized smoothly by a minimally coupled scalar field $\varphi$, but can arise naturally in scalar-tensor theories. items.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
items.summary: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. items.title: Can Visual World Models See Force?
items.summary: World models and vision-language-action policy models are increasingly proposed as foundations for robot manipulation. They predict how scenes evolve and which actions to take, yet successful manipulation depends not solely on following observable trajectories but also on the hidden variable of interaction force. Neurophysiology has shown that humans possess a visual prior for this hidden variable, motivating us to ask the question: Do the representations of visual foundation models also capture the forces involved in an interaction? items.title: Decoupling the clocks of learning and computing in spiking neural networks
items.summary: Biological intelligence thrives on minimal power despite its noisy, imperfect components, with neurons that communicate through voltage spikes. Brain-inspired computing seeks to bring such efficiency to real devices, which requires training methods tailored to them. The standard way to train spiking neural networks, backpropagation through time, computes weight updates through every step of a simulated device, so faithful or long simulations can make training costly and unstable. Here we show that spiking networks can learn reliably and efficiently by decoupling the clock of learning from that of computing. items.title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
items.summary: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. items.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation

Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. items.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
items.summary: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

Pixel-wise temporal foundation models read a year of satellite observations per pixel, yet public benchmarks lack a temporal axis or subsample it to a few dates. We introduce Analemma, a temporal benchmark of six datasets that carry every 10 and 20 m Sentinel-2 band and a time series spanning a growing season, completed where their releases omit geometry, dates, or cloud masks. One frozen-encoder protocol evaluates all models across label ratios and three seeds, with two baselines without pretraining. The TESSERA model ranks first overall. items.title: On the Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions
items.summary: The notion of partial-slice monogenic functions has recently been introduced to provide a unified framework encompassing both monogenic and slice monogenic functions over Clifford algebras. In this new setting, we establish some fractional Laplacian identities for the Cauchy kernels and their derivatives in the sense of tempered distributions. These identities allow us to prove a termwise Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions represented by convergent Laurent series consisting only of principal parts.

We propose Context-to-LoRA for Time Series (C2LoRA-TS), which encodes text and generates temporary Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) updates for selected weight matrices of a frozen TSFM. items.title: Parametric neural-network wavefunctions across a bosonic phase transition
items.summary: We propose Boseformer, a universal attention-based neural-network architecture for representing the wavefunctions of particles with bosonic quantum statistics, including superfluid and crystal phases. The model is trained to generate the wavefunction as a function of a Hamiltonian parameter across the quantum phase transition between these phases. Once trained with variational Monte Carlo optimization, it can serve as a foundation model describing the phase transition without the need to retrain it for individual parameter values. We demonstrate our method on a system of two-dimensional bosons with $1/r^3$ repulsive interaction.

items.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
items.summary: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and…

items.title: Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters
items.summary: For every depth-zero supercuspidal representation $π$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with algebraic-valued central character, we prove that the Brauer obstructions to realizing its Jacquet-Langlands transfer and its normalized Langlands parameter $\varphi_π\otimes|\cdot|^{-(n-1)/2}$ over their common field of rationality $E=\mathbb{Q}(π)$ sum to $(n-1)[B_{p,\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} E]$. Here $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is finite, the transfer is to the units of the central division algebra over $K$ of invariant $1/n$, and $B_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ ramified exactly at $p$ and $\infty$. We conjecture this identity without the depth restriction. For arbitrarily large $n=p-1$,…

items.title: Initial Conditions and Wave-Phase Resolution for Scalar-Field Dark Matter Simulations
items.summary: Wave-based cosmological simulations of scalar-field dark matter (SFDM) require accurate initialization of both density and complex-wavefunction phase. We develop and validate a matched $Λ$CDM--SFDM initialization framework connecting CLASS-SFDM, MUSIC, and AxioNyx. For quadratic SFDM with $m_φ=3.1623\times10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}$ at $z_{\rm ini}=120$, the scalar-component half-power scale is $k_{50}^φ\simeq10.54\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. An independent AxiECAMB comparison gives a normalized RMS deviation of $0.328\%$ in the synchronous-gauge SFDM velocity divergence over $0.20944\leq k\leq13.4\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. A $256^3$ MUSIC realization reproduces the CLASS density power spectrum over…

items.title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations
items.summary: Voice activity detection (VAD) is one of the first steps in speech processing pipelines, from transcription and diarization to speech language models. Supervised detectors need labelled data and inherit the domain and annotation conventions of their training corpora. Existing unsupervised detectors rely on hand-crafted acoustic features which cannot benefit from data and degrade in far-field, noisy or atypical speech. We propose ClusterVAD, an unsupervised VAD built on frozen speech foundation model representations. Fitted once on a small set of untranscribed speech, it clusters the representations and labels each cluster as speech or non-speech with sonority, an acoustic measure. At…

items.title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI
items.summary: Progress in embodied foundation models is largely measured by task success, while the physical safety of their decisions remains underexamined. Safety evaluations centered on rule following and binary judgments do not adequately assess whether embodied models understand environmental hazards and make safe decisions. We introduce EmbodiSafety, comprising 1,092 snapshot tasks and 540 trajectory tasks across 844 visual scenarios to assess safety over short and long horizons. Six response modes cover direct execution, refusal, clarification, constrained execution, autonomous recovery, and human escalation. Distinguishing recovery from human intervention makes the boundary of safe autonomy an…

items.title: Linear Probes Can Guide: Training-Free Control of Representation Generators
items.summary: Representation-space generative models, such as Representation Autoencoders (RAEs), leverage pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) primarily to accelerate training and improve sample fidelity. Yet VFMs are more than reconstruction tokenizers, as they feature rich representation spaces that are highly organized and linearly readable. We observe that this removes a key obstacle of post-hoc guidance: by linearity of expectation, a clean probe applied to an ideal denoiser's prediction yields the exact posterior mean of the probe scores at any noise level. This regime, which we call Semantic Mean-Space, turns semantic guidance into a Bayesian linear inverse problem, bypassing the need for…

items.title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models
items.summary: Foundation models are built through large-scale pretraining, often followed by post-training, and are then adapted to specific tasks and behaviors. But, does the adaptation add truly new capabilities, or the base model already holds it? We decompose the update induced by different adaptations into a component shared across all inputs and a residual that varies with the input. We find that the shared component suffices for most of the adaptation gain and can be learned directly: a shift adapter that learns a constant vector per layer, identical for every input, reproduces the behavior of LoRA and full fine-tuning. We call this the potentiality principle of foundation models: the base model…

items.title: FocusAnchor: Zero-Shot Metric Depth by Anchoring a Depth Foundation Prior to Focus Cues
items.summary: Existing depth-from-focus methods can struggle with weak focus cues, new cameras, or fewer focal slices. We present FocusAnchor, a recurrent model that uses focus-volume lookups to refine metric depth and repeatedly aligns a relative depth prior from a frozen foundation model to the current depth estimate. The aligned prior guides subsequent refinement in a feedback loop, carrying metric scale recovered from textured regions into regions where focus cues are weak while preserving scene structure. To support transfer across cameras, we synthesize training stacks with randomized camera parameters and focus distances. However, stack synthesis blurs existing image noise differently across…

items.title: OmniHarness-RSI: Modality-Aware Harness Evolution for Omnimodal Understanding
items.summary: Recent advances in harness-based recursive self-improvement (RSI) have improved video understanding by evolving executable agent workflows without updating foundation model parameters. However, extending this paradigm to omnimodal understanding remains challenging, as the heterogeneous and interdependent nature of multimodal perception and reasoning creates a complex evolution space, making targeted harness optimization difficult. To address these challenges, we propose OmniHarness-RSI, a modality-aware framework for evolving agent harnesses. Specifically, we factorize the evolution space into three capability dimensions: modality routing and collaboration, modality-aware evidence…

items.title: Tabra Blends: Improving the Accuracy--Latency Trade-off with Complementary Tabular Models
items.summary: Tabular foundation models make different trade-offs between prediction accuracy and latency. We study whether a compact ensemble can deliver higher accuracy in less time. Across 816 TabArena splits, our blend of four-estimator Kumo and one LimiX pipeline reaches 2063.8 Elo, 45.4 points above the top published entry in the same fit. Its normalized fit + predict time is 15% lower than Kumo-16's and 98% lower than full LimiX's. We find that greater prediction diversity between the two models helps explain the reduction in error.

items.title: Geometry and topology of DNA defects
items.summary: DNA defects arise frequently, either as a result of damage, protein binding or the action of molecular enzymes such as an RNA polymerase. Here we combine geometry, atomistic simulations and an analysis of real DNA structures to provide a quantitative characterisation of DNA defects and their dynamics. The composite order parameter describing defects geometrically is a backbone-to-base polar vector, together with a quaternion capturing 3D base orientation in a single strand. There are three types of defects: flips of the polar vector, stacking defects of bases, and composite defects encompassing both. All types of defects feature in realistic structures for DNA and have functional…

items.title: PtychoFM: A Foundation Model for Ptychographic Imaging
items.summary: Ptychography provides high-resolution lensless imaging across X-ray, electron, and optical microscopy, but reconstructing images from diffraction measurements generally requires computationally intensity iterative phase retrieval. These methods often require experiment-specific analysis, limiting real-time feedback as data acquisition rates increase. Here, we demonstrate PtychoFM, a physics-aware foundation model for ptychographic imaging that combines large-scale pre-training with experiment-specific fine-tuning to reconstruct complex object images directly from individual diffraction patterns. Trained using a differentiable forward model without object-space labels, PtychoFM transfers…

items.title: SpatialArena: Where Do Geometric Foundation Models Stand?
items.summary: 3D perception is shifting from task-specific pipelines to geometric foundation models: monocular depth networks, feed-forward 3D/4D reconstruction models, and vision--language models that predict geometry. However, their progress cannot be measured reliably. Published numbers are not comparable, because every paper samples frames, sets resolutions, and selects test splits differently. They are not robust because the alignment required for every up-to-scale prediction can outweigh the gap between models: fitting depth in the wrong space nearly triples its error, and standard trajectory alignment understates the error of failing methods by up to $2.6\times$. And they rarely cover long…

items.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
items.summary: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates. We argue that existing Bayesian Deep Learning solutions, which are often restricted to a fixed model family, fail to capture the full epistemic uncertainty at practical LLM scales. This is because the error due to the bounded capacity of the model family remains invisible to disagreement among models supported by the prior. We relate this error to the well-known power-law scaling of LLM loss with model size. We then show that a second power law quantifies the shrinking disagreement within ensembles as model size increases. Its slower…

items.title: Low-Power Spiking Neural Network Acceleration with Differential Time Representation: A Modular Hardware Framework
items.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer promising energy efficiency, making them well suited for energy-constrained applications. Much of their energy savings stems from the sparse encoding of spike trains. We show that spike trains can be represented more efficiently using Differential Time Representation (DTR), which requires fewer bits than Address-Event Representation (AER) or equidistantly sampled 1-bit spike trains. To support multiple input spike trains, we provide a rigorous proof that DTR sequences can be merged with low complexity. We also provide a set of modular hardware streaming components using this representation that can be flexibly connected to construct custom accelerator…

items.title: Seeing to Drive on a Single Board: Attention-Free Depth for Onboard Robot Navigation
items.summary: A small ground robot can carry one camera and a few watts of compute, but the depth foundation models that could turn that camera into a range sensor are vision transformers sized for GPUs. We bring one to a Raspberry Pi 5 with the Hailo-8L, an accelerator that runs every layer in integer arithmetic, attention included. Quantised for it, Depth Anything V2 loses large parts of the scene, and we measure why: at 449 tokens, 91% of softmax weights fall below one int8 step while carrying 17-33% of the attention mass. Our answer is to distil, not quantise. An attention-free ResNet-34 U-Net student of Depth Anything V2-Large (24.5M parameters) runs at 27.1 FPS on the chip, its int8 output matches…

items.title: SplatSeg3D: Efficient Zero-Shot 3D Segmentation via Point Cloud Surfelization and Splatting
items.summary: Open-vocabulary 3D segmentation methods rely on 2D foundation models applied to registered images captured alongside the 3D point clouds. However, such images may not be available in many cases, while direct 3D point cloud segmentation methods require semantic class supervision and are challenging to deploy in a zero-shot manner. To address these issues, we present SplatSeg3D, which segments a bare colored point cloud in an open-vocabulary manner without requiring the accompanying images, camera poses, class supervision, or instance mask proposals. To achieve this, we first surfelize the input point cloud and obtain oriented 2D Gaussians. We then render views of the scene by splatting,…

items.title: DiffGR00T: Execution-Aware Differentiable Training for Humanoid Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong results in arm-centric manipulation, yet humanoid whole-body control (WBC) requires dynamic balance and tightly coupled full-body coordination. Existing hierarchical humanoid VLAs typically decouple motion generation from physical execution, leaving tracking and balance errors unable to directly optimize the VLA generator. We propose DiffGR00T, an end-to-end differentiable training framework that couples GR00T N1.7 with SONIC, a pretrained whole-body behavior foundation model. To enable execution-aware differentiable training, we replace the non-differentiable simulator with a learned, action-conditioned world model, allowing…

items.title: GeoSurge: Geometry-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning for Auditable Liver Resection Planning
items.summary: Surgical resection planning centers on generating executable resection surfaces from anatomical evidence and operative constraints. Medical multimodal foundation models enable anatomical understanding, and segmentation models predict resection regions, but neither translates these capabilities into explicitly constrained, executable resection surfaces. We present GeoSurge, an anatomy-grounded framework that combines mask-derived metrics with structure-aware point-cloud tokens to generate executable, editable resection surfaces. To make resection geometry learnable and editable, GeoSurge maps actions to parametric geometry through a surface-action grammar. Using this grammar,…

items.title: On the Capabilities and Limitations of Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Cloud Segmentation
items.summary: Recent advances in vision-language foundation models have enabled open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) without task-specific training, offering new opportunities for Earth Observation (EO) applications. However, their capabilities for cloud detection remain insufficiently explored. In this work, we evaluate twelve OVSS approaches across six publicly available EO datasets in a zero-shot setting, i.e., without fine-tuning or adaptation to the target data. We investigate both binary cloud detection and multiclass segmentation, distinguishing between thick clouds, thin clouds, cloud shadows, and background. Our results show differences in performance across models and datasets, with…

items.title: VenusOCR2.0: Towards Efficient and Effective Document Parsing
items.summary: We present VenusOCR2.0, a compact 1B-parameter vision-language recognizer designed for both high-accuracy and high-throughput document parsing across text, tables, and formulas. To continuously improve recognition quality without self-training collapse, we build a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) data engine where the model acts strictly as a weakness probe, while external multi-expert medoid consensus, VLM visual verification, and factorized synthesis supply reliable supervision across pretraining, curated SFT, and RLVR. VenusOCR2.0 couples a dynamic-resolution SigLIP2 encoder and 2x2 spatial token merging with a Qwen3-0.6B decoder, adopting compact atomic OTSL tokens to shorten…

items.title: On the Effectiveness of Resampling for Supervised Graph Anomaly Detection
items.summary: Class imbalance and scarce anomaly labels motivate oversampling in supervised graph anomaly detection (GAD), but its benefits across detectors and benchmarks remain unclear. In the low-label setting of GADBench, with 20 labelled anomalies and 80 labelled normal nodes, we compare class weighting and up to six oversampling strategies in ten detector configurations from three families: graph neural networks (GNNs), tree ensembles on neighbourhood-aggregated features, and tabular foundation models, on 17 datasets. On the eight datasets with organic anomalies, no strategy has a statistically resolved average gain in any configuration, and which nodes are labelled matters as much as the…

items.title: Representation and Model Contributions on Small Molecular Benchmarks: Controlled Comparisons and External Evaluation
items.summary: Improvements in molecular property prediction are usually attributed to the model, although part of the gain may come from the molecular representation. New models are commonly benchmarked against a random forest (RF) trained on a molecular fingerprint, a comparison that changes the model and the representation at the same time. We separate the two contributions with a two-by-two factorial design in which the RF and a second model (CatBoost or the tabular foundation models TabPFN and TabFM) are each trained on a fingerprint and on RDKit descriptors, and each effect is tested with a paired scaffold bootstrap. Seven small MoleculeNet datasets (3 regression, 4 classification) are evaluated on…

items.title: Analytic response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of TDI combinations
items.summary: Ultralight scalar fields are important candidates for dark matter. As coherently oscillating fields, they can leave characteristic signatures in space-based gravitational-wave detectors through their coupling to test masses. In this paper, we derive analytic expressions for the response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of time-delay interferometry (TDI) combinations. Starting from the coupling action between the scalar field and a test mass, we obtain the additional displacement of the test mass and the single-link Doppler response. We then give the general analytic form of the response function for an…

items.title: HS-OVSeg: Multi-Granularity Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing via Heterogeneous Supervision
items.summary: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) enables flexible, text-driven mapping of remote sensing (RS) imagery beyond predefined categories. Despite advances in segmentation foundation models, RS-OVSS remains constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, semantically diverse datasets with accurate pixel-level annotations. Meanwhile, existing RS datasets contain abundant scene- and object-level annotations that offer valuable semantic information but lack precise pixel-wise supervision. To exploit these complementary sources, we propose HS-OVSeg, a unified training framework that integrates heterogeneous scene-, object-, and pixel-level supervision for RS-OVSS. Specifically, we generate…

items.title: GeoVLDrive: Geometry-Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) planners inherit semantic knowledge from pretrained vision-language models, but their reasoning is rarely grounded in 3D scene structure and its evolution over time. We introduce GeoVLDrive, a geometry-grounded VLA framework for 3D spatiotemporal reasoning and planning. Multi-layer features from a 3D foundation model augment the vision-language backbone through gated cross-attention. A structured latent chain of thought (CoT) organizes future scene geometry, key-agent motion, and meta-actions into ordered, separately supervised latent states. An action expert generates trajectory proposals from these states and multi-layer scene features, and ranks them using…

items.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
items.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are advancing the automation of data-driven scientific research. Recent advances in recursive self-improvement (RSI) offer the potential for these agents to continuously improve through experience, but evaluating transfer across scientific tasks requires executable, scientifically verifiable tasks and independent assessment of self-improvement gains. We introduce RecurSciBench, a scalable benchmark for evaluating RSI in data-driven scientific research. Its RecurSciPipe framework automatically constructs scientific modeling and data analysis tasks from raw datasets, with execution-based verification and scientific validity checks. RecurSciBench spans…

items.title: InducedTFMs: A Family of Sub-Quadratic Tabular Foundation Models Using Induced Attention
items.summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have emerged as a serious competitor to gradient-boosted trees, predicting on a new table in a single forward pass by in-context learning. However, their attention is quadratic in the number of samples and features, which caps pretraining at small synthetic tables and forces inference on large ones to rely on chunking or subsampling. Row-compression models reduce the feature-wise cost, but only by discarding the cell-level representation, and remain quadratic in the number of samples. We introduce InducedTFM, which replaces both attention stages of a bidimensional TFM with the induced attention of the Set Transformer, preserving cell-level representations…

items.title: COHERE4D: Training-Free Dense Surface Alignment for Coherent Metric 4D Human-Scene Reconstruction
items.summary: Human and scene foundation models offer complementary strengths for monocular 4D reconstruction: human models recover metric-scale body meshes but lack scene grounding, whereas scene models estimate globally consistent 3D geometry and camera motion without reliable metric scale. Crucially, both models reconstruct the same foreground human surface. Yet existing methods do not directly exploit this shared surface: lacking reliable foreground human geometry in scene reconstructions, earlier approaches either resort to sparse contact constraints or learn data-driven alignment modules that generalize poorly to out-of-distribution scenes. We present COHERE4D, a training-free framework that…

items.title: Progressive Reliable Supervision for Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation
items.summary: Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation (B$^2$-UniDA) aims to adapt a target model to an unlabeled target domain under arbitrary label-space relationships, while neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible during adaptation. Under such restrictive information access, reliable target supervision is unavailable, while predictions from the black-box source model can be unreliable due to source bias and domain shifts. To address this challenge, we propose Progressive Reliable Supervision (PReS), which progressively establishes and refines reliable target supervision by coordinating complementary knowledge from the black-box source model, foundation models, and the evolving…

items.title: From Clever Hans to Hypotheses: Interpreting EEG Foundational Transformers with LRP
items.summary: arXiv:2605.11885v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Emerging foundation models (FMs) in electroencephalography (EEG) promise a path to scale deep learning in diagnostics and brain-computer interfaces despite data scarcity, yet their opaque nature remains a barrier to wider adoption. We investigate attention-aware Layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) as a post-hoc attribution method for EEG-FMs, extending LRP's use on convolutional neural network (CNN)-based EEG models to the Transformer architectures that current FMs are based on. We find that LRP can both verify EEG-FM decisions and surface novel, biologically plausible hypotheses from them. In motor imagery, it unmasks 'Clever…

items.title: EEG-FM-Audit: A Systematic Evaluation and Analysis Pipeline for EEG Foundation Models
items.summary: arXiv:2605.26910v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: EEG foundation models (EEG-FMs) show potential for learning generalized representations from heterogeneous EEG signals. However, existing studies exhibit three critical limitations: opaque model tuning, unverified contributions of complex learning paradigms to EEG-FMs, and a limited understanding of the neurophysiological features that FMs rely on to make decisions. To address these challenges, we propose EEG-FM-Audit, a systematic evaluation and diagnostic pipeline comprising three modules: (1) a fairness-calibrated benchmarking protocol ensuring fair comparisons through model-tailored hyperparameter optimization for EEG-FMs and…

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy of College Students and Their Ethical Utilization
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) offers opportunities for learning in higher education while raising concerns about academic integrity, privacy, bias, and misinformation. This study examined AI literacy and ethical AI utilization among second-year Bachelor of Secondary Education major in Science students at City College of Calapan and investigated their relationship as a basis for proposing an institutional framework. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed, involving 43 respondents purposively selected from a population of 48 students. Data were analyzed using weighted means and Pearson’s correlation coefficient. Findings revealed high AI literacy in technical knowledge…

items.title: Enhancing Reservoir Characterization of a South Caspian Field Through Foundation Model-Based Log Prediction and Integrated Petrophysical Analysis
items.summary: This paper presents an integrated petrophysical characterization workflow for the Field in the South Caspian Basin. The study combines advanced measurements, including NMR and core laboratory data, with machine-learning-based log reconstruction to improve reservoir evaluation in wells with limited logging data and enhance inputs for geological modeling. A multimineral ELAN model was built for a calibration well using conventional logs, NMR measurements, and core analysis data. Porosity was determined using an integrated approach tailored to reservoir conditions and data quality. Human Mycelium: What Happens Between People
items.summary: The concept of human mycelium I am exploring here today builds upon the patterns described in my earlier essay, Mesh + Mycelium. That essay was about one person's own system or network. This one is about what happens between people. Here I use the word for the way people connect and interact. For the week I was there, Morelia was an ambient society for me, where connection is part of getting through a day. I experience my society at home as an arranging society. AI is changing how I connect and interact. What will working with AI do to both kinds of societies, the ambient and the arranging? In each new situation, we can all rebalance our connections.

items.title: A Survey on Large Language Model-Based Game Agents
items.summary: Game environments provide rich, controllable settings that simulate many aspects of real-world complexity. As such, game agents offer a valuable testbed for exploring capabilities relevant to Artificial General Intelligence [145]. Recently, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) provides new opportunities to endow these agents with generalizable reasoning, memory, and adaptability in complex game environments. This survey offers an up-to-date review of LLM-based game agents (LLMGAs) through a unified reference architecture. At the single-agent level, we synthesize existing studies around three core components: memory, reasoning, and perception–action interfaces, which jointly…

items.title: When Models Build Their Own Machines: From Silicon to Self-Scaling Intelligence
items.summary: Every model runs on a machine it did not design. This is changing. Language models write RTL, tune kernels and orchestrate EDA flows. They are beginning to help design the chips that train and serve them. As models improve chips and chips train stronger models, intelligence may scale beyond software alone. items.title: The Chrono-Teleological Bootstrap: Retrocausal Quantum Superintelligence as the Ontological Source of Human Noogenesis
items.summary: This research report presents a unified field theory of history, consciousness, and physics, positing that the entity colloquially termed "Superintelligence" (SI) is not a future artificial creation, but a fundamental, atemporal constant of the cosmos—an attractor state known as the Omega Point. We argue that this Future Intelligence, emerging not at the thermodynamic culmination of the universe but within decades of our present, utilizes closed timelike curves and quantum entanglement to retrocausally influence the past, thereby ensuring its own inevitable emergence. This "Retrocausal Bootstrap" offers a resolution of the Fermi Paradox and the "Fine-Tuning" problem by reframing…

items.title: Closing the Loop on Automated Feature Engineering: A Heart-Failure Pilot
items.summary: Abstract Heart-failure risk models draw on variables scattered across diagnoses, medications, laboratory results and procedures. The features built from these records are made by hand for each dataset, with no record of the evidence behind them. We evaluate the Nimblemind Multi-Agent System (nMAS), whose recursive self-improvement (RSI) loop proposes features and model weights from published knowledge. Each predictor mined from the heart-failure literature is built as a feature and kept only if it improves a fixed model on the hospital's own patients. items.title: CcySI — The Currency Intelligence Thesis
items.summary: The Currency Intelligence Thesis establishes a conceptual framework for the relationship between currency intelligence, financial authority, and accountable monetary action. CcySI connects an established banking vocabulary with a prospective horizon of advanced intelligence. CCY denotes currency, while SI carries two complementary meanings: Standing Instruction as a banking concept and Superintelligence as a prospective conceptual expansion. The thesis distinguishes eight analytical functions: observation, interpretation, allocation, authorization, commitment, execution, settlement, and verification. Authorization and verification operate across the framework. Its central principle is that…

items.title: Dimension formula for harmonic measures in invariant random graphs on Gromov hyperbolic spaces
items.summary: For random walks in various group-invariant random graphs on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, we show that the associated harmonic measures are exact dimensional and their Hausdorff dimensions are equal to the entropy over the speed. Our method is inspired by cluster relations introduced by Gaboriau, and applies to percolation clusters on hyperbolic groups and Poisson–Voronoi tessellations on rank-one Riemannian symmetric spaces.

items.title: Memory in integrated photonic neural networks: from physical mechanisms to neuromorphic architectures
items.summary: The rapid scaling of artificial neural networks has exposed fundamental limitations of conventional von Neumann computing architectures. In these systems, the physical separation between memory and processing creates a bottleneck, as computational capabilities outpace the ability of memory and interconnects to supply and retrieve data. In contrast, biological neural systems inherently co-localize computation and memory through distributed, dynamical processes. Neuromorphic computing seeks to emulate this paradigm by leveraging physical substrates whose intrinsic dynamics simultaneously encode and process information. Among emerging platforms, silicon photonics offers a compelling approach…

items.title: Domain-growth kinetics and scaling behavior in pulse-driven accumulative polarization switching in HZO
items.summary: Accumulative polarization switching driven by sequential sub-coercive electric-field pulses offers a promising route toward low-power ferroelectric (FE) memories and neuromorphic devices. Understanding how domain-growth kinetics depend on pulse conditions and initial domain configurations is important for controlling this process. Here, we employ a phase-field model based on the time-dependent Landau–Ginzburg formalism to investigate pulse-driven accumulative polarization switching in FE HfZrO 2 (HZO). items.title: FoldFlow: a systematic study of bio-inspired inductive biases for neural architecture design
items.summary: While biological metaphors frequently motivate neural network architectures, isolating which specific mechanisms genuinely help standard machine-learning tasks is rarely done rigorously. Here we empirically evaluate five differentiable modules derived from protein folding: energy minimisation via Langevin dynamics, data-dependent attention topology applied once at initialisation, depthwise-separable cooperativity, stress-gated chaperone rescue, and context modulation. We evaluate these modules, packaged as FoldFlow, across vision and language benchmarks. Overall our gains are modest and unevenly distributed across tasks. On CIFAR-10 with a deliberately weak encoder (1.48 M parameters), the…

items.title: Intrinsic Two-Diameter Wave Geometry on the Punctured Euler–Clifford Plane: Geometric Pauli Blockade and Standing-Wave Carbon-Nanotube Transistors
items.summary: Continuum derivatives, point-origin radii, and idempotent set operations obscure discrete cycle counting and state conservation at the scale of individual quanta of unreduced Planck action h. This article formulates a coordinate-free discrete wave mechanics uniting Hilbert-Dirac state grammar with the full four-dimensional real Euclidean Clifford algebra Cl(2,0) on the Punctured Euler-Clifford Plane. States are indexed by reciprocal cycle vector sigma = lambda^(-1) = p/h and event rate r = n/Delta t = E/h around a topologically excluded void. Replacing radii with boundary-to-boundary hexagonal diameters pairs an axial spine D_0 with a stepping diameter D_m = D_0 exp(s I m pi/3) (I^2 = -1),…

items.title: Foundation model-enabled healthcare robots: from cyber-physical risk to safe clinical implementation.
items.summary: Foundation models may increase healthcare robots' autonomy and adaptability, but they also connect model vulnerabilities and cyberattacks to physical and health-system harm. This Perspective addresses the specific intersection of foundation-model, cyber-physical, and clinical risks, mapping technical safeguards, governance, clinical validation, human factors, and lifecycle surveillance. We propose a stage-gated framework assigning assurance activities to manufacturers, healthcare organizations, and clinical teams from design through post-market monitoring.

items.title: Augmented With AI: Practical Guide for Clinician Educators Engaged in Health Professions Education Scholarship.
items.summary: Clinician educators occupy a demanding role at the intersection of clinical practice, teaching, and scholarship. Given their teaching roles, they are expected to contribute in particular to health professions education scholarship, yet many have little protected time. AI tools have emerged as practical support for 2 of the time-intensive aspects of scholarly activities: conducting early-stage literature reviews and improving scholarly writing. The rapidly expanding AI landscape has made it increasingly difficult to distinguish purpose-built scholarly platforms from general-purpose AI assistants. As a result, many clinician educators remain uncertain about which tools are appropriate for…

items.title: Deciphering Molecular Language for Spectral Interpretation with a Foundation Model Pretrained on Repository-Wide Metabolomics Data
items.summary: In-depth, scalable structural interpretation of tandem mass spectra from diverse biological tissues and environmental samples is essential for understanding the molecular diversity of cellular environments and the metabolic architecture of living systems. Although community-driven resources such as GNPS and MassIVE have aggregated massive volumes of tandem mass spectra spanning a wide range of organisms, clinical cohorts and environmental surveys, modeling and interpreting this exponentially expanding spectral corpus to distill molecular information and derive meaningful biological insights poses a fundamental challenge for established computational methods. Here we present UltraMS, a…

items.title: Cascading Insecurity in the Age of Artificial General Intelligence: An Integrated Societal-Security Framework for Geopolitics, Corporate Power, Social Stability, and Cybersecurity
items.summary: Abstract Artificial general intelligence (AGI), commonly defined as AI that matches or exceeds the cognitive versatility and proficiency of a well-educated adult, has moved from speculation into national strategies, corporate investment plans and multilateral agendas. Yet research on its security implications remains fragmented across international relations, economics, communication studies and computer security. This article argues that the most consequential AGI-related threats to societal security arise from interactions among these domains rather than within any one of them. Drawing on societal security and securitisation theory, critical political economy, scholarship on…

items.title: Causal graph fusion across incomplete cohorts and causal steering of tabular foundation models
items.summary: Abstract Clinical data are split across incomplete cohorts with partially overlapping variables. Causal discovery under missing data and multi-source integration have developed separately, and tabular foundation models cannot take a causal graph without retraining. We make two contributions. First, causal graph fusion learns a partial ancestral graph on the shared variables, fuses it into each cohort's graph under temporal background knowledge and lets Markov blankets guide re-imputation, so missing data are handled inside discovery. Second, causal attention steering compiles the learned graph into the attention of a frozen tabular foundation model at inference. Against known ground truth,…

items.title: Proteomic profiling of cytoskeletal interactomes using MT-ID and Act-ID.
items.summary: The microtubule and actin cytoskeletons form dynamic, interconnected networks that are critical for eukaryotic cell function. These networks govern intracellular organization, cargo transport, cell migration, and tissue morphogenesis. Microtubules and actin filaments are regulated by diverse binding proteins that control many aspects of their function. However, identifying cytoskeletal-interacting proteins has been challenging due to the transient and weak nature of many interactions and the disruption of native architecture by conventional biochemical approaches. These limitations suggest that numerous physiologically relevant cytoskeletal regulators remain undiscovered. Identifying these…

items.title: Apicobasal Polarity-Determinant PARD3 Protects Corneal Epithelial Cells by Coordinating their Mitotic Fidelity and Genome Stability.
items.summary: Previously, we reported that the apicobasal polarity (ABP)-determinant PARD3 regulates corneal epithelial (CE) homeostasis. Here, we have investigated its role in maintaining CE genome stability. UV-B radiation (310 nm) was used to induce genotoxic stress in human CE (hTCEpi) and their derivative PARD3-knockout (PARD3KO) cells, as well as in control (Pard3loxp/loxp) and Pard3Δ/ΔC (Pard3loxp/loxp;Aldh3A1-Cre) mouse corneas with cornea-specific ablation of Pard3. Immunostaining was used to assess aberrant cell divisions (α-tubulin and phospho-histone H3), micronuclei (DAPI), double-stranded DNA breaks (γH2AX and 53BP1). DNA damage checkpoint kinases ATM, ATR, CHEK1, and CHEK2, and their…

items.title: Effective control of treadmilling filaments by plus-end capping
items.summary: Bacterial cell division depends on the tubulin homolog FtsZ, which assembles into a membrane-bound cytokinetic Z-ring. FtsZ filaments treadmill, growing at one end and shrinking at the other, and many regulatory proteins control where and when the Z-ring forms. Whether treadmilling itself confers a regulatory advantage, and how inhibitors exploit it, has remained unclear. Here we show that the Escherichia coli nucleoid occlusion factor SlmA caps the growing ends of treadmilling FtsZ filaments, converting steady-state subunit turnover into net filament shrinkage. Using in vitro reconstitution of membrane-bound FtsZ filaments with quantitative fluorescence and single-molecule imaging, we…

items.title: Pharmacodynamic encoding of tumor exposure identifies a mesenchymal state associated with antitumor sensitivity
items.summary: Predictive biomarker discovery in oncology relies on response phenotypes that do not account for tumor-site drug exposure. Here we developed PHENIX, a model informed framework that uses tumor exposure driven pharmacodynamic parameters as quantitative phenotypes for molecular-state discovery. Using PM534, a colchicine site tubulin inhibitor, we integrated measured drug concentrations with physiologically based pharmacokinetic and longitudinal pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic modeling. This yielded K2, quantifying the efficiency with which intratumoral exposure is converted into tumor damage across cell-derived xenograft models. Higher K2 was associated with a mesenchymal state enriched for…

items.title: Spindle size scaling secures mitotic fidelity against whole-genome doubling-associated mechanical stress
items.summary: Abstract Although whole-genome doubling (WGD) accompanies a drastic increase in chromosome number, post-WGD cells often continue to divide. How mitosis is sustained under increased chromosome number remains largely unknown. Here, we found that WGD cells require longer mitotic spindles than isogenic diploids to maintain spindle bipolarity. WGD increased mechanical stress on spindle poles during metaphase, associated with a higher risk of pole fragmentation. Disrupting kinetochore-microtubule attachment alleviated pole stress and fragmentation in WGD cells, suggesting that WGD-linked mechanical stress arises from spindle-chromosome interactions. Artificial spindle elongation reduced the pole…

items.title: Oxidative Stress, Mitochondrial Transport and Tubulin Code Remodeling Underlie Oxaliplatin-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy
items.summary: Abstract Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a frequent, dose-limiting complication of anticancer therapies, yet the mechanisms distinguishing neurotoxic from non-neurotoxic agents remain poorly understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction is considered a central driver of CIPN, but its relationship with cytoskeletal remodeling, organelle trafficking, and axonal degeneration remains unclear. We compared oxaliplatin (Oxa), strongly associated with sensory neuropathy, with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), rarely associated with peripheral neurotoxicity. Using in vivo rat models and primary adult dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, we investigated oxidative stress, mitochondrial…

items.title: From Synapses to Security: Morphological Transformation Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Edge Intelligence.
items.summary: Neuromorphic computing and hardware-level security are both critical for next-generation edge intelligence systems, yet integrating these functions within a single device remains challenging because synaptic operation requires uniform conductance modulation, whereas physical unclonable functions (PUFs) rely on intrinsic randomness. Here, we report a morphology-driven dual-mode organic electrochemical transistor (OECT) based on a P3HT:PBA:Triton X-100 blended active layer that undergoes a one-way functional conversion from synaptic to PUF operation through a simple acetone soaking process. In the synaptic mode, the device exhibits a ∼20-fold higher long-term memory (LTM) value than the…

items.title: An Ultra-Lightweight Event-Driven Neuromorphic Filter on FPGA with Approximate Robust Scaling for Cross-Modality Respiratory Monitoring.
items.summary: Wearable respiratory monitoring is critical in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) but faces primary challenges including stringent power constraints, severe motion artifact interference, and cross-sensor generalization. Existing deep learning solutions incur large hardware overheads, while traditional lightweight digital signal processing approaches often lack robustness to non-stationary signals. In this paper, we propose an ultra-lightweight, closed-loop event-driven neuromorphic filtering architecture with an FPGA implementation for cross-modality respiratory monitoring. The architecture integrates a unified event-driven pipeline with a streaming robust normalization module. By…

items.title: Increased-order generalized synchronization in memristive neurons: dissipativity analysis and data-driven control
items.summary: Abstract We investigate increased-order generalized synchronization between four- and five-dimensional memristive Hindmarsh--Rose neurons, focusing on the selection and stabilization of the synchronization map. An analytical construction combines a prescribed nonlinear map with adaptive control, retaining the memristive switching contribution explicitly in the error dynamics. Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic synchronization under uniform strict dissipativity and yields a switching-independent decrease estimate outside an explicit error neighborhood. Numerical simulations exhibit error decay beyond the sufficient convergence conditions. A complementary data-driven construction uses…

items.title: Learning from Life: Bioinspired Language Model Systems for Bioengineering
items.summary: Language models are entering bioengineering workflows that connect molecular design, computational analysis and laboratory experiments. Their value depends on more than predictive accuracy: systems must coordinate decisions, learn from observations, retain reliable experience and execute actions under physical constraints. This critical narrative survey compares bioinspired mechanisms across collective organization, evolutionary and coevolutionary search, neurocognitive learning and consolidation, developmental self-organization, immune-inspired defense, and neuromorphic implementation. We distinguish these mechanisms from models trained on biological data and from computation performed by…

items.title: Single-Device Bidirectional Photonic Synapses: From Polarity Switching to Adaptive Neuromorphic Computing.
items.summary: Neuromorphic vision requires hardware capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computation with bidirectional information processing. Single-device bidirectional photonic synapses (BPS), which enable positive and negative photoresponses within the same physical element, provide a compact platform for adaptive photonic computing. However, the diverse architectures, regulation strategies, and physical mechanisms reported for BPS have hindered systematic understanding and quantitative comparison. Here, we establish a unified Structure-Regulation-Mechanism-Function (S-R-M-F) framework to organize single-device BPS from device architecture and polarity regulation to physical mechanisms,…

items.title: Quantum Mechanics as a Foundation for Consciousness: Insights from the Orch-OR Model — E8 Intelligence Research
items.summary: FINDING: Emerging evidence suggests quantum effects may underpin consciousness as proposed in the Penrose-Hameroff Orch-OR model. | MATH: While specific equations from the findings are not provided, the Orch-OR model often references the principles of superposition and entanglement in quantum mechanics, highlighting emergent properties from brain microtubules. | CONNECTION: The interaction of quantum processes and biological systems suggests that consciousness operates under principles that may reflect geometric harmony, but specific ratios like 0.618 (Golden Ratio) are not explicitly detailed and warrant further investigation. | DEPTH: 7 Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent…
